status: The crew's bodies (roadmap 8.10, docs/crew/10_BODIES_AND_VOICES.md): the sizes of a seated crewman for simcore/crew_body.hpp (the bodies Unreal draws, the reach check of the cabin layout) and tools/blender/build_crew_body.py (the meshes). Each seat's rest posture and gaze.
source: winter_biomech; gost_12_2_032_78; sam3d estimates where a block says so
notes: Body frame of data/cabins/<system>.json. Lengths are fractions of the stature, so a taller or shorter crewman only changes stature_m. The sitting eye height this gives (0.79 m above the seat) and GOST's seat height (0.43 m) put the floor 1.22 m under a station's eye point: the Osa cabin's floor is 0.62 m and its bench eyes 1.83 m above the ground, 1.21 m apart.

body.source: sam3d estimate (a conscript of the 1980s; no published figure found yet)

fractions.source: winter_biomech ch. 4: segment lengths as fractions of the height H (after Drillis and Contini, 1966)
fractions.notes: Standing heights of the eye, shoulder joint, hip joint (greater trochanter), knee and ankle; upper arm 0.186 H, forearm 0.146 H, hand 0.108 H, foot 0.152 H; breadths across the shoulders and the hips.

seat.source: gost_12_2_032_78 Table 2 (seat height, men: 430 mm); the hip joints above the seat and the eye ahead of them are sam3d estimates

limits.source: gost_12_2_032_78 §4.4 (displays read rarely: within 60 degrees of the line of sight with eye and head movement); the bend at the hips (sitting, standing), the twist of the shoulders, the turn on the seat, the crouch and the head's pitch are sam3d estimates

motion.notes: How fast a hand goes to a control, how long it stays after moving it, and how far from a panel he stands when he has to get up for it. The time to stand up and step is drill time and lives in the crew data (data/crew/<system>_crew.json, standing).

seats.notes: Hands on the steering wheel and feet on the pedals when he isn't reaching for a control; looks out through the windscreen.
Looks out through the windscreen when nothing calls him.
Watches the range indicator (the Osa); the PU-12M's operator-plotter his air-situation map.
The PU-12M: watches the IT-45 beside the operator.
The PU-12M: looks ahead over the KP-4.
